fields.features_heading: What the Lot Needs Before the Trunks Open
fields.features_subheading: A trunk or treat sign up sheet decides where each car parks and who stays to clean up. Emergent builds it as a small app.
fields.feature_1:
A sheet drafted from one sentence

Describe the event, such as 30 trunks in a church lot with three volunteer shifts. Emergent builds the sign-up form and its database, then changes both when you ask in plain English.
fields.feature_2:
Spots and themes claimed only once

A numbered parking spot or a trunk theme drops off the list as soon as a family takes it. The next family picks from what is left, so two pirate ships never park side by side.
fields.feature_3:
Shifts that close when they are full

Set how many people each volunteer shift needs. A full shift stops taking names, and the organizer sees which shifts still have open slots in the week before the trunks line up.
fields.feature_4:
Reminder emails before the night

The app emails each trunk host and volunteer ahead of the event with a spot number, arrival time, or shift. Move the start time and the change reaches everyone who signed up.
fields.feature_5:
Every sign-up in a database you own

Sign-ups land in a database you own, with no cap on responses. Next fall's organizer opens last year's hosts and themes there instead of hunting for a paper sheet in a closet.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can move to your own repo

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository. A school district can host the sign-up sheet beside its other event pages and keep building on it from there.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Lots, Four Ways to Fill the Sheet
fields.tab_content_1:
Themes stay with whoever claimed them, one per trunk

Ridgefold Community Church lines its east lot with 30 numbered trunk spots, run by Noreen Vasquerra. So far, 26 of the 30 spots are claimed. When the Tillery family picks Under the Sea, the sheet shows the Prudhomme family holds it at spot 9 and asks for another theme. Each host gets an email with the spot number.
fields.tab_content_2:
Volunteers who signed up all get a day-before email

Brookhaw Elementary's PTO needs 14 volunteers on the night: 6 for setup, 4 at the candy table, and 4 for cleanup. Chair Jubal Cassidine sees 12 of 14 slots taken, with cleanup still 2 people short. The day before the event, each of the 12 volunteers gets an email with the shift and the time to arrive.
fields.tab_content_3:
For 212 kids, each trunk needs 212 pieces of candy

Gwen Ilsley stopped guessing at candy for the Mabrey Volunteer Fire Company's lot. Families RSVP with how many kids are coming, and 87 families have listed 212 kids. The sheet counts one piece per child at every trunk, so the 18 trunk hosts each get an email asking for at least 212 pieces, 3,816 in all.
fields.tab_content_4:
When voting closes, Haunted Barn leads with 41

Durrance Motors hands out candy from 22 trunks on its sales lot, and families vote for the best one from their phones. Voting closes at 7:30 pm with 148 votes in. Haunted Barn wins with 41, ahead of Dragon's Lair at 33 and Pirate Ship at 29. Sales manager Cosmo Lunetti announces it from the showroom steps.

fields.howto_title: How to Plan Your Trunk or Treat Sign-Up Sheet
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a trunk or treat sign up sheet that settles trunk spots and shifts before the night, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Measure the lot before anything else
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask hosts only what you will use
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Split the volunteer work into shifts
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Add a family RSVP with a kid count
fields.howto_step_1_des: Count the parking spaces you can give to trunks before the sheet goes out. Leave a lane for families on foot and a gap at each end, then number every space on a simple map. That count becomes the cap on trunk sign-ups.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask each trunk host for a contact email, the car, the theme, and whether the trunk hands out candy or non-food treats. Leave out anything nobody will look at on the night, such as the car's make or a long bio.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List the jobs that keep the night running, such as setup, a greeter at the entrance, the candy table, and cleanup. Give each shift a start time and a headcount. A parent scanning the sheet then sees where help is still missing.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask families how many children are coming and their ages. The kid count sets how much candy each host brings, and the ages show whether a quieter corner with trunks for toddlers is worth setting aside.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Choose who hears what, and when
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide which emails the sheet sends: a confirmation with the spot number, a reminder the day before, and a notice if rain moves the event indoors. Send each one only to the people it concerns, not the whole list.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send a test sign-up from a phone
fields.howto_step_6_des: Sign up as a made-up family from your own phone, then as a host and as a volunteer. Check that a taken theme is refused, that a full shift closes, and that the confirmation shows the right spot. Delete the test rows afterward.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Post the link in the parent newsletter and the church bulletin about 3 weeks before the date. Close trunk sign-ups 2 days ahead, which leaves time to print the lot map and hand the final count to your volunteers.

faq_plan.q: What is a trunk or treat sign up sheet?
faq_plan.ref: trunk or treat sign up sheet
faq_plan.a: A trunk or treat sign up sheet is the list that settles which cars take part in the event and where each one parks. At a trunk or treat, candy or other treats are handed out of the trunks of vehicles. The sheet records who hosts each trunk and the parking spot it gets, plus anyone helping out on the night.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a trunk or treat sign up sheet?
faq_plan.ref: trunk or treat sign up sheet
faq_plan.a: Describe the event to Emergent's AI form builder in a sentence or two: how many trunk spots the lot holds, what each host enters, and any volunteer shifts. Emergent builds the sheet and its database. Ask for changes in plain English afterward, such as a field for a rain date.

faq_plan.q: How many trunk spots should a trunk or treat sign up sheet offer?
faq_plan.a: Offer as many spots as your lot holds with a walking lane marked, and no more. Compare that number with the family RSVPs as they come in. With a big crowd and a small lot, ask each host for more candy instead of squeezing in extra cars. Sign-up sheets built on Emergent put no cap on the number of RSVPs.

faq_plan.q: What should families fill in on a trunk or treat sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Ask each family for a name, a contact email, and how many children are coming with their ages. Make a food allergy field optional. Questions about how families heard about the event fit better in a short follow-up, written like audience survey questions. On Emergent, every RSVP stays in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How much candy should a trunk or treat sign up sheet ask each host to bring?
faq_plan.a: Ask for one piece for each expected child, at each trunk, then add a margin for walk-ins who never RSVP'd. A host expecting 150 kids might bring 180 pieces. If the line loops back for a second pass, put that in the reminder email so no host runs out halfway through the night.

faq_plan.q: How do I mark allergy-friendly trunks on a trunk or treat sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Ask each host whether their trunk gives out non-food treats, such as stickers or glow sticks, and show the answer as a tag next to that spot on the lot map. Parents can then see which trunks to visit before they arrive. Keep the question optional for hosts who are unsure what they will bring.

faq_plan.q: Should a trunk or treat sign up sheet include volunteer shifts?
faq_plan.a: Yes, once the night needs more than trunk hosts. Put setup and cleanup on the same sheet, each with a headcount, and send every volunteer a short brief with the one job they own. Afterward, a three-question debrief, kept as short as learning and development survey questions, shows what was unclear.

faq_plan.q: Can hosts change their spot after filling in a trunk or treat sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you build the sheet to allow it. Each confirmation email can carry a link that reopens the host's own entry, and a spot or theme they give up goes back on the list for the next family. Lock changes once trunk sign-ups close, which keeps the printed lot map accurate.

faq_plan.q: How do I tell everyone on a trunk or treat sign up sheet that rain moved the event?
faq_plan.a: Send one email to everyone on the sheet with the new time or the indoor location. Because every sign-up sits in one database, one message reaches hosts and families alike. Emergent can build the sheet to send that email and show an in-app alert on the sign-up page.

faq_plan.q: Can a trunk or treat sign up sheet run a best trunk vote?
faq_plan.a: Yes. List every registered trunk by spot number and theme on a vote page, and let each family pick one from a phone. Hide the running count until voting closes to keep early leaders from swaying the rest. Keep the vote to one quick pick, the way game survey questions keep players moving.

faq_heading: Trunk or Treat Sign-Up Sheet FAQ

plan.angle: The top 10 for trunk or treat sign up sheet is printables and editable Etsy, Canva and Pinterest sheets: one grid of blanks for name, car and theme. None of them can stop two families claiming the same theme, remind volunteers, or tell trunk hosts how much candy to bring once the RSVPs are in. This page shows the sign-up sheet as a small app for four real jobs: a church assigning parking spots and themes, a PTO filling volunteer shifts, a fire company sizing candy from family RSVPs, and a car dealership running a best trunk vote. The FAQ covers how many trunks to plan, what to ask families, allergy-friendly trunks, timing and weather changes.
